subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Opium Wars: Tea's Deadly Trade
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Opium Wars: Tea's Deadly Trade.

hook.text: Britain's tea addiction created a huge trade deficit with China. The solution? Flood China with opium to balance the books.

buildup.text: By the 1830s, Britain imported millions of pounds of Chinese tea but had little that China wanted to buy in return.

discovery.text: Britain grew opium in India and smuggled it into China—creating millions of addicts and reversing the trade deficit.

twist.text: When China tried to stop the opium trade, Britain declared war. Two Opium Wars forced China to accept the drug trade.

climax.text: Tea's demand fueled one of history's most devastating drug crises. The cup of tea in London had a dark trail back to China.

punchline.text: A cup of tea, a trail of opium, two wars. Demand has consequences.

quiz.question: Why did Britain sell opium to China?
options: To balance a trade deficit caused by massive tea imports from China
